Amalgamation of Ahascragh and Fohenagh (juvenile 1999, adult 2002). Home club of Cathal and Pádraic Mannion. First adult title since amalgamation: Galway Junior C 2009-10. Galway and Connacht Intermediate champions 2016; All-Ireland Intermediate Club runners-up 2016-17. Historic note: Fohenagh (old club) won Galway senior hurling in 1959 and 1960 — those are predecessor titles, not amalgam titles.
East Galway hurling club formed by amalgamation of Ahascragh and Fohenagh. Also searched as Fohenagh or Ahascragh. Fohenagh (old club) won Galway in 1959 and 1960 (see historic predecessor).

We brought the kids to Salthill the night Galway won. Maroon everywhere. Someone started singing 'The West's Awake' near the diving boards. The little ones still talk about the fireworks.
First time I saw Joe Canning for Portumna I was still in primary school. Sideline cut from halfway — silence, then the net shook. Portumna kids still practice that strike.
Granny still cries when Joe Connolly's speech comes on. She was in a neighbour's house in Ballinasloe — no big screen, just the radio and tea going cold.
First championship day at Pearse Stadium
My dad brought me to Pearse Stadium with a paper flag and a bag of crisps. I didn't understand scores yet — only that Galway in maroon meant roar.
Every child had a jersey on. We replayed the final with plastic hurleys at little break. Conor Whelan was the most popular name to be.
When Cathal and Pádraic lined out for Ahascragh-Fohenagh, the whole parish followed. Intermediate glory felt like an All-Ireland on our own pitch.
Tony Keady stories on the bus
On the way to underage matches the older lads told Tony Keady stories. We didn't know the politics yet — only that he was the best centre-back anyone had seen.
After another county final the cars crawled through Kilchreest with horns going. David Burke waved like it was Croke Park all over again.
Our street still talks about the Connollys. Joe's speech is on a fridge magnet. Hurling here is family history.
